decoder_payload.reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every finite-dimensional real inner-product space E equipped with its Borel measurable structure and canonical volume (including dimension zero), every function V:E->R, every alpha,beta in the nonnegative reals, and every real eta, suppose alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C^2, and for all x,v in E the diagonal Hessian satisfies alpha*||v||^2 <= D^2V(x)[v,v] <= beta*||v||^2. Suppose eta>0 and beta*eta<=1.
Define mu as normalized volume tilted by exp(-V). For independent X with law mu and Z with standard Gaussian law on E, let Y=X+sqrt(eta)Z. Let J be the actual law of (X,Y), nu the second marginal of J, Lambda the actual law of (Y,2X-Y), and F(x,y)=(x,2x-y). Define P on real L^2(J) to be the specified actual conditional orthogonal projection onto the subspace measurable with respect to the second coordinate.
Then mu, J and nu are probability measures. There is a single measurable Markov probability kernel S:E->Prob(E) such that for EVERY y in E, S(y) is normalized volume tilted by exp(-V((y+x)/2)-||y-x||^2/(8 eta)) as a measure in x. The actual joint measure Lambda disintegrates as Lambda.fst compProd S; both its first and second marginals equal nu.
There is a single real linear isometry U:L^2(J)->L^2(J) whose representative obeys Ug=g composed with F, J-almost everywhere for every g in L^2(J). U is involutive and its associated continuous linear map is self-adjoint. There is a single real linear isometry M:L^2(nu)->L^2(J) whose representative obeys Mu=u composed with the second-coordinate projection, J-almost everywhere for every u in L^2(nu). There is a single bounded real linear map T:L^2(nu)->L^2(nu). These choices S,U,M,T precede the arbitrary input u.
Write A=P U P and B=(I-P) U P, where products mean operator composition with the rightmost factor applied first. For every u in L^2(nu), P(Mu)=Mu, M(Tu)=A(Mu), and ||Tu||<=||u||. The chosen representative of Tu equals y->integral u(x) S(y)(dx), nu-almost everywhere. For nu-almost every y, both u and x->u(x)^2 are integrable under S(y). The function y->Var_{S(y)}(u) is integrable under nu, where Var_rho(u)=integral (u(x)-integral u(t)rho(dt))^2 rho(dx). Moreover integral Var_{S(y)}(u) nu(dy)=||B(Mu)||^2=||u||^2-||Tu||^2.
Here every L^2 space consists of strongly measurable square-integrable real functions modulo almost-everywhere equality. Operator equalities live in these quotient spaces; the displayed representative equalities are only almost everywhere. No all-y fiber integrability or all-y conditional-integral identity for arbitrary rough L^2 inputs is asserted.

typical_misreadings: Treating finite-dimensional E as implying finite-dimensional L2(J) or L2(nu).
Replacing the actual mu,J,nu,Lambda by arbitrary caller-supplied probability laws or replacing P by an assumed projection.
Reading the existential S,U,M,T as new objects chosen separately for each u.
Replacing the kernel identity at every y by an AE identity, or upgrading AE fiber integrability and representative equality to every y.
Identifying a chosen L2 representative with a globally pointwise-defined version free of null-set dependence.
Adding centering, compact support, smoothness, weak-H1 membership or gradient control for u.
Reading the exact averaged variance identity as a Poincare inequality, positive spectral gap, strict contraction or quantitative mixing rate.
Mistaking alpha,beta bounds on V for additional higher-derivative bounds or properties of arbitrary observable u.
Replacing S(y) by a Gaussian law; its density contains V((y+x)/2) as well as the quadratic term.
Reading IsCondKernel as an input certificate rather than a proved actual disintegration conclusion.
Using packet compiled=true as this decoder own compiler verification or source-fidelity judgment.

No simultaneous null set working for every L2 input.
No strict norm decrease, spectral gap, Poincare/LSI constant, mixing/iteration count or convergence rate.
No derivative, gradient-energy or Sobolev estimate on u.
No executable sampling algorithm, numerical discretization guarantee, query complexity or unbounded-cost theorem.
No source theorem identification, proof reconstruction, independent compilation or source-fidelity admission.
